summary: Phase 4 adds real deterministic Organ and Synth renderers with six organ models, source-family/filter/envelope/LFO processing, and one shared EffectsGraph; all 33 tests and pnpm typecheck/lint/build pass. The implementation is materially stronger offline than in its browser path, but the hardware/UI surface is still a generic Phase 3-style control map, many required Phase 4 controls are absent or no-op, Program/scene/split/morph state is not applied back to engine controls, and Web Audio noteOn uses a single generic oscillator (and only the focused/first synth layer). This is a plausible modelled-audio prototype, not a substantially complete Stage 4 Organ/Synth integration.

evidence: stage4-desktop.png preserves the continuous red chassis, 73-key E-to-E keybed, six section order and Program/Synth-only OLED placement from inherited evidence.
The capture remains structurally close to the reference, although the caption still says 'PIANO PHASE 02' and the Organ/Synth panels are simplified.
Organ has nine drawbars and a few model/percussion/rotary controls; Synth has one OLED and a compact generic oscillator/filter cluster.

Required three synth-layer indicators, register/preset/live LEDs, filter/envelope menus, voice/arp mode indicators and engine focus states are not visibly represented; displayed Synth OLED is static 'SYNTH / WAVE' or 'SYNTH / ARP'.

renderOrganNote contains six named harmonic models, nine drawbar values, Farf register gating, B3 percussion, key click, vibrato/chorus, rotary speed/drive/close-mic, octave, levels and two-layer summing; phase4 boundary tests verify model and representative-control differences.

WebAudio noteOn builds only simple sine/saw oscillators, does not implement model-specific percussion/click/vibrato/rotary behavior or rotary acceleration, and the UI only drives Organ A. Preset/live, sync, zones and morph behavior are state fields rather than complete workflows.

renderSynthNote includes Samples/Analog modes, Pure/Sync/Multi/Super/Misc/Wave/FM categories, all listed filter names, tracking/drive, three envelopes, LFO destinations, unison/vibrato and deterministic gate/arp gain pattern; tests exercise a subset.

Extern produces no sound, most source categories collapse to a small waveform mapping, Osc Ctrl is ignored for several categories, and range/inversion/hold/run/keyboard-sync/priority/glide/legato are not rendered as the manual describes. Browser noteOn is one generic oscillator and only uses layer A.
OrganEngine and SynthEngine can receive the inherited graph and ProgramState contains organ/synth metadata; a test verifies graph identity and metadata serialization.

Program load/store does not hydrate OrganEngine/SynthEngine controls; scene switching and morph application operate inherited Piano/effect destinations only; split/zone routing is not consulted by Organ/Synth noteOn; presets and UI focus remain Piano-oriented.
Offline renderers produce measurable spectral/time-domain differences for the six Organ models and representative Synth sources, filters, envelopes and LFO/arp settings (phase4 tests pass).

The audible browser path bypasses those renderers: Organ creates generic oscillators and Synth creates one generic oscillator with no filter/envelope/source-family graph, so model/source controls do not reliably alter live sound as claimed. No recording/sample provenance is claimed, which is truthful but less faithful to the Nord sample library.
Both engines accept the same EffectsGraph instance; graph creates organ-A/B and synth-A/B/C buses, ordered chains, master limiter and one destination; null-context tests prove shared identity.

Organ noteOn routes all active layers to whichever layer is focused, and Synth noteOn routes only A (and routes C focus to synth-B); no per-layer effect targeting or zone-aware routing is exercised for live Organ/Synth voices.
Native voices use short gain ramps, stop/disconnect on noteOff and dispose/allNotesOff; deterministic fallback is available and all technical gates pass.

There is no Organ/Synth voice allocator/limit, sustain or proper per-note release lifecycle, browser stress/latency audit, or clipping/CPU evidence; synth/organ repeated release calls clear all voices rather than preserving independent notes.
Main maps a handful of Organ A drawbars/model/percussion/rotary and Synth A level/wave/filter/envelope/LFO/arp buttons into engine setters.

Required B/C layer controls, Organ register/preset/sync/zone/octave/pitch-stick and most percussion/vibrato/rotary options, Synth mode/category/filter type/envelope/LFO destination/voice/arp menu controls are missing; many visible controls are generic toggles that only update local state/program metadata.
ProgramState serializes organ and synth metadata and the Program OLED reports name/category/list/dirty state.
Loading a Program does not apply its organ/synth metadata to the engine instances; Synth OLED is hard-coded to SYNTH / WAVE or ARP and no contextual model/source/filter/arp values are displayed.
Canonical Program state includes seven layer IDs, zones, scenes, morphs, master clock and effect chains.

Only Piano layer scene switching and Piano morph destinations are wired in main.tsx; Organ/Synth controls do not follow Program enabled/level/zone state, split note routing, scene transitions or morph input paths, and master clock is not propagated to engines from Program state.
Inherited Phase 1-3 tests plus phase4.test.ts pass (33 tests); pnpm typecheck, lint and build pass.
The visual audit explicitly says no fresh browser interaction capture was possible, so console/runtime regression evidence for Organ/Synth gestures is limited.

Organ and Synth are separate typed modules with deterministic render boundaries and injectable AudioContext/EffectsGraph; graph ownership prevents additional destination contexts when composed by App.

Engine controls are duplicated from ProgramState and are not synchronized; browser and offline implementations diverge substantially, and focused-bus routing is hard-coded rather than layer/zone based.
Code is readable and modular; feature matrix lists Phase 4 IDs and direct tests cover model/source spectra, representative DSP, graph identity and serialization.

Only four shallow Phase 4 test cases cover many dozens of required behaviors; tests do not assert browser bindings, layer B/C behavior, Program hydration, split/morph/scene integration, or true WebAudio model processing. Feature-matrix claims exceed what tests exercise.
pnpm test/typecheck/lint/build all pass; build is small (~241 kB JS) and deterministic null-context fallback avoids device dependence.

No fresh browser audit was captured; generic oscillator paths, unbounded Organ/Synth voice maps, and allNotesOff-on-any-key-release behavior leave layered rapid-play, cleanup, latency and console cleanliness unverified.

issues.title: Live WebAudio path does not implement the tested Organ/Synth engines
issues.evidence: OrganEngine.noteOn creates generic sine/saw partial oscillators without percussion/click/vibrato/rotary; SynthEngine.noteOn creates one oscillator and ignores source/filter/envelope/LFO/arp controls. Browser users therefore do not hear most claimed controls.

issues.title: Program, scenes, splits and morphs do not hydrate or route Organ/Synth state
issues.evidence: ProgramState stores metadata, but App only applies scene/morph changes to Piano; Organ/Synth noteOn never checks zones/splits and ProgramStore load has no engine synchronization.

issues.title: Required hardware inventory is largely decorative/generic
issues.evidence: The UI exposes only Organ A and Synth A subsets. B3/Farf/pipe register/preset/sync, Synth B/C, filter type/tracking, three envelope pages, LFO destination/group, voice priority/glide, arp menu/range/hold/sync controls are absent or local toggles.

issues.title: Layer routing is incorrect for active/focused layers
issues.evidence: Organ routes all active layers to the focused organ bus; Synth noteOn always uses layerA and maps focused C to synth-B, preventing independent per-layer effect chains.

issues.title: Deterministic tests under-cover the required contract
issues.evidence: 33 tests pass, but phase4.test.ts has four cases and does not exercise live AudioContext processing, browser controls, layer B/C, registration/preset workflows, split/morph/scene routing, priority/glide/hold/clock semantics or performance stress.

issues.title: Visual evidence is inherited rather than a Phase 4 interaction audit
issues.evidence: stage4-visual-audit.md states no in-app browser was available; screenshot caption remains 'interactive surface / piano phase 02' and Synth display is static.
